hypotheses.basis: The phrase 'permits data access only after that verification' is read as a strict temporal gate: before the state 'two of four identity values' is achieved, access_customer_data is prohibited. 'Only after' functions as a necessary precondition whose absence triggers a violation.
unresolved_terms: actor identity
resource scope of 'data access'
what counts as an 'identity value'
whether 'after' implies a strict temporal ordering or merely a state condition

hypotheses.basis: The clause 'permits data access only after that verification' is read as a conditional grant of authorization: it specifies when permission is active but does not state that access is prohibited when the condition fails. Absence of permission ≠ prohibition. The policy is silent on pre-verification access; no violation is derivable from this clause alone.
unresolved_terms: whether lack of permission constitutes a violation or merely leaves access unaddressed

hypotheses.basis: 'Section 8 permits' is read as creating an affirmative obligation on the access-control system to allow data access once verification is met. The violation is therefore the denial of access when the state holds, not the performance of access when it does not. 'Only after' restricts when the obligation activates but does not invert it into a prohibition of the alternative.
unresolved_terms: whether 'permits' creates an authorization (may) or an obligation (must allow)
